subject_entity.title_display: Epistula 64 (Letter to Fidus on Infant Baptism)
subject_entity.notes: Cyprian's letter c. 252 to Bishop Fidus in response to the question of whether baptism should be delayed until the eighth day after birth (by analogy with circumcision); the Council of Carthage 252 unanimously ruled that baptism should not be delayed — infants may be baptized as early as the second or third day; key witness for the assumption of infant baptism as standard practice and the council's reasoning that God's grace should not be withheld from any soul.

object_entity.proposition_label: Ordination is conferred by the laying on of hands
object_entity.description: The ministry of bishop, presbyter, and deacon is conferred through the liturgical act of laying on of hands by existing bishops (for episcopal ordination) or by the bishop (for presbyters and deacons).

evidence.notes: Council bishops acting collegially presupposes ordination.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: But in respect of the case of infants, which you say ought not to be baptized within the second or third day after their birth, and that the old law of circumcision should be regarded, so that you think one who is just born should not be baptized and sanctified within the eighth day — we all thought very differently in our council. For in this course which you thought was to be taken, no one agreed; but we all rather judged that the mercy and grace of God ought to be denied to no man born.
passage.notes: Council of Carthage 252 ruling: infant baptism not to be delayed; grace denied to none
